name: Carlos Patel

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to employers, AI companies, unions or government, and your answers are confidential. What is a typical day at work?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 43, have an MBA, and lead twelve people who resolve service-credit claims at a large telecom company. When a network outage closes a shop’s payment terminal, we check the outage record, decide a fair credit and explain it to the customer. I have done this for ten years and other managers call me on the difficult cases. The staff are good, but a neat account number can hide a shop that could not take any sales.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My wife works in a school library, and our children are nine and fourteen. We have a mortgage and about four months of expenses saved. My pay is normal for a manager here, and there are some similar service jobs nearby. I use an approved AI tool occasionally for a plain first draft, but I never let it decide a credit amount.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the team AI Plateau changes the speed of routine replies, not our duty to check the outage record. A customer needs a credit based on what actually happened.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my job and salary hold. Four months saved helps if the library has a short week, though the mortgage still takes its share. I would not spend time defending the job against a minor drafting tool.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep the second review on credits above a day’s service and ask handlers to note which claims needed a call to a shop. If a new reply feature arrives, I’d test it on ten settled outage cases before allowing it into live letters. We would keep the monthly transfer to our emergency account while both wages arrive.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about my own work. I still keep an eye on the mortgage, as I did before this conversation.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What did a shop call change?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: One café lost its payment terminal for half a Saturday. The system counted a two-hour outage, but customers had left and the lunch trade was gone. We gave a larger credit after speaking to the owner.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you tell the team the tool helped?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Of course, if it writes a clear first letter. I would also show the call that changed the amount. The team should get credit for that work rather than vanish into a faster reply number.

say: **AI Plateau** changes reply speed, not the duty to check outages.
I would tell staff that **customer calls** can change a fair credit.
think: My **job and salary** look steady under a minor drafting change.
The **mortgage** and possible short library weeks still need watching.
do: **Keep** second review on larger service credits in 2026.
**Test** a new reply feature on ten settled outages before live use.
**Continue** monthly emergency transfers while both wages arrive.
feel: I feel **calm** about work while still watching mortgage bills.
S0.quote: The system counted a two-hour outage, but customers had left and the lunch trade was gone.
fieldNote: His **four-month reserve** and stable skilled role support calm in a mild scenario.
He values the **customer call** that changes a credit amount, not just letter speed.

steps.text: Keep second review on service credits above one day
Test reply feature on ten settled outage claims before live use
Continue monthly emergency transfers while both wages arrive

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say Steady Disruption will write replies, check records, book callbacks and answer simple claims. I would ask the company and staff council to agree on case loads and an appeal route before anyone cuts handlers.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, our screen work is exposed and even a strong team could become smaller. I have built trust here, but headquarters could decide one manager can oversee more claims with software. Four months saved gives me some time, not certainty about my current salary.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This quarter I’d take twenty closed disputes where a person changed the credit and compare them with the company’s approved AI checker. I’d bring missed cases to the staff council and ask them to negotiate paid appeal training for handlers. If management posts shrink, I’d apply for a posted service-quality manager role only if its pay covers our mortgage and its hours fit the younger child’s school run.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious. I can defend the work with evidence, but I cannot promise headquarters will keep all twelve handlers.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would go in the evidence?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The café that lost lunch trade, with the outage time and the owner’s call recorded separately. A quick automated credit might be technically correct and still miss the real complaint. I would show the two amounts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you ask handlers to learn the checker?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only on paid time, after we know what it misses. I would ask for a trainer and a real appeal job for anyone moved off routine claims. A course without a post would be decoration.

say: **Claims automation** needs negotiated case loads and a human appeal route.
I would show **changed credits** that a simple outage time missed.
think: Headquarters might put more claims under **one manager**, shrinking my team.
Four months saved gives time, but my **salary** is still at risk.
do: **Compare** twenty changed-credit cases with the approved AI checker this quarter.
**Bring** missed cases to the staff council for paid appeal training talks.
**Apply** for service quality only with mortgage pay and school-compatible hours.
feel: I feel **anxious** about a smaller team and uncertain salary.
S1.quote: A course without a post would be decoration.
fieldNote: He uses **case evidence** and a staff council rather than claiming expertise alone guarantees jobs.
A **service-quality vacancy** must offer mortgage pay and hours that suit the younger child.

steps.text: Test approved AI checker against twenty credits changed after customer calls
Give missed-credit cases to staff council for paid appeal training talks
Apply for posted service-quality role only with mortgage pay and school-compatible hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the team AGI by 2028 could settle claims, write letters and check outage records as well as us. We need a written staffing date and a named person who can reverse a wrong credit.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Full thinking AI in 2028 reaches my desk and a service-quality manager’s reports. Robots that can do hands-on network repairs arrive around 2031, so they do not give us extra years. I expect our claims team to shrink, and my post might go even though I know the hardest cases. The four-month reserve and other local employers help, but a mortgage needs wages.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next week I’d ask the staff council to seek severance figures and a written human-appeal rule. I’d apply for two posted customer-resolution roles only if their salary and hours cover our mortgage and children’s care. If AGI arrives in 2028 and I’m cut, I’d accept a confirmed offer only after checking the actual contract; otherwise we would use the reserve for essential bills while I searched.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about losing a team I’ve trained. I am not out of options, but four months would pass faster than people think.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell your children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say I might work at another office, but they are staying in school for now. The younger one worries about pickup, so my wife and I would not change it before we had a real rota. I would not present a vacancy as a job offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who should hear a wrong credit appeal?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A person with authority to change the payment, not a chatbot repeating the policy. I would show the café case to that reviewer. A screen cannot carry the embarrassment of telling the café owner that lost lunch trade did not count.

say: **AGI by 2028** needs staffing dates and a person able to reverse wrong credits.
I’d ask the staff council for **severance figures** before cuts.
think: Claims and service-quality reports face **2028 AGI**, before repair robots around 2031.
My expert post might go, though **four months saved** gives a short search.
do: **Ask** the staff council next week for severance and human appeal terms.
**Apply** for posted resolution roles only with mortgage pay and child-compatible hours.
**Accept** a confirmed post-2028 offer only after checking pay, care and real contract terms.
feel: I feel **anxious** about job loss, with some time and nearby options.
S2.quote: A screen cannot carry the embarrassment of telling the café owner that lost lunch trade did not count.
fieldNote: He separates **2028 thinking exposure** from physical network repair robots around 2031.
His **high skill** does not guarantee a post, while four months saved avoids immediate missed bills.

steps.text: Ask staff council for severance figures and written human appeal rule
Apply for posted resolution roles only with mortgage pay and child-compatible hours
Accept confirmed offer after 2028 only if pay care and contract terms fit

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2031 gives five years to decide what a fair appeal looks like when software sets the first credit. I would ask for a funded route into independent complaints work, with real authority.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My present work and a complaints manager’s writing both face AGI in 2031. Robots doing hands-on repairs come around 2034, but our screen roles do not wait for them. Five years lets me build more savings if both wages hold; it does not promise an appeal vacancy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: From January 2027 I’d handle one paid independent review a month under the complaints head if my manager covers my team. I’d take an accredited complaints course only if the company pays the fee and gives me work hours. After 2031 I’d apply for an appeals lead post only if it still lets me change a wrong credit and pays enough for the mortgage and school timetable.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious, though I have time to practise a narrower skill. I would not leave a good team for a title that only reads the AI answer aloud.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the complaints head teach?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: How to separate a technical outage record from the customer’s business loss without promising money the contract does not allow. I know our credits, but an independent review asks me to test my own side. I would need someone to mark where I was unfair.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the company pays the fee but not the time?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would not enrol. My wife works school hours and we have two children; evenings are not an empty slot. I would ask for paid study time or keep learning on the cases I can handle at work.

say: **Five years** can fund independent reviews with real appeal authority.
I would need **paid study time**, not only a course fee.
think: Claims and complaints writing face **2031 AGI**, before repair robots around 2034.
More savings depend on **both wages**, and a vacancy is uncertain.
do: **Handle** one paid review monthly from January 2027 only with team cover.
**Enrol** in complaints training only with employer-paid fee and paid work hours.
**Apply** after 2031 only for appeals authority with mortgage pay and school hours.
feel: I feel **anxious** about the desk, with time to test independent review.
S3.quote: I would not leave a good team for a title that only reads the AI answer aloud.
fieldNote: He tests **independent review** under supervision and names a real skill gap in challenging his own team.
Course **fees and hours** are separate conditions; an enquiry would not count as enrolment.

steps.text: Handle one paid independent review monthly only with claims-team cover
Enrol in complaints course only with funded fee and paid study hours
Apply after 2031 for appeal vacancy only with reversal authority mortgage pay and school hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2036 gives a decade to write fair appeal rules and show staff which jobs remain. I would ask the company and staff council to publish the pay and decision rights for each role.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: By 2036 our children will be about nineteen and twenty-four. If our wages hold, we could pay down more of the mortgage and build over four months of savings. My claims and appeals reports still face AGI in 2036; robots for physical repair work arrive around 2039. A longer runway helps, but I cannot bank a future vacancy today.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep second reviews on large credits and add a small amount to savings only after both wages, mortgage and school bills clear. I’d ask the staff council yearly for real appeal openings and their authority. Before 2036 I’d take a paid independent-review post only if salary and family hours work; after AGI arrives I’d remain only while I can reverse wrong credits and cover our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about the distant change. Our bills are secure for now, but an appeal title without authority would not be worth chasing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How much could you add?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Maybe forty in a full month when the library has all its hours. I would transfer it only after the mortgage and school costs clear. If a child needs something unexpected, we would skip it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would a fair role description say?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Who can change a credit, how many cases one person handles and what the pay is. I would take those terms to the staff council. A job without the power to correct a wrong decision is only a waiting room.

say: A **decade** should bring published appeal jobs and decision rights.
I would ask the **staff council** to show the pay for each role.
think: Both wages could reduce the **mortgage** and grow savings.
Claims and appeals reports face **2036 AGI**, before repair robots around 2039.
do: **Keep** second reviews on larger credits in 2026.
**Save** forty only after both wages, full library hours and mortgage/school bills clear; skip transfers for unexpected child costs.
**Take** an appeal post only with workable salary and hours; stay after 2036 only with reversal authority and bill pay.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about distant change while current bills remain secure.
S4.quote: A job without the power to correct a wrong decision is only a waiting room.
fieldNote: His **moderate cushion** makes a decade workable; extra saving needs both wages, full library hours and no unexpected child cost.
He uses **staff council terms** to keep a future appeal role accountable for pay and decision rights.

steps.text: Keep second reviews on credits above one day of service
Save forty with both wages, full library hours, paid bills and no unexpected child costs
Ask staff council yearly for appeal openings pay and decision rights
Take posted appeal role only with salary and hours fitting household bills

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because a claims desk could shrink before a genuine human appeal role exists. A written date, real severance and paid independent-review work would help. Four months saved gives us time to make a choice, not authority to change a wrong credit.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask the café owner whose terminal failed during lunch whether a two-hour credit settled the loss. A two-hour outage credit did not replace the café’s lost lunch trade. Someone must have the power to change the amount.

headlineQuote: A two-hour outage credit did not replace the café’s lost lunch trade.
portrait: **Carlos, 43**, is an MBA-trained senior service-credit manager leading twelve handlers at a large telecom company.
His **typical pay**, school-library wife, four-month reserve and some local jobs support a mortgage and two children.
He uses **AI occasionally** for drafts but checks outage claims against what customers actually lost.
He is **calm** under AI Plateau, anxious about possible cuts and seeks paid independent-review authority with household pay protected.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could shrink his claims desk before a real human appeal job exists.
whatWouldHelp: A written **date**, severance and paid independent-review work would help.
